kind: Predeclared single-factor fused-baseline development trial 3 (final allowed recipe trial; development only)
factor: model.value_feature_gradient true -> false (value-head inputs detached; value regression no longer updates actor-partition features vlln, vl_self_attention, state_encoder)
selected_from_data: Trial 2: actor grad norm ~44 every window (always clipped to 1.0) while |policy_loss| ~1e-3 and PPO clip_fraction ~0.3%; actor update size grows over time; decline is reward-independent and monotone. The value head shares actor features (ppo.py _features/_values), so value-loss gradients plausibly dominate the actor update direction. Value warmup would not address late drift; lr 3e-7 would only slow it.
unchanged_relative_to_trial_2: actor lr 1e-6, value_lr 1e-4, native LIBERO-10 profile (8 envs on 8 GPUs, 4 updates per 128-decision window), fused AdamW fp32_master, clip 1.0, betas/eps/decay, checkpoint, aligned_200, seed 17
success_criterion: PASS iff every completed aligned_200 evaluation at update >= 80 (80, 160, 240, 320) has success >= 0.885 (>= 177/200) AND mean episode_steps <= 339.10. Failing any completed evaluation FAILS the trial (cancel). The update-80 evaluation must complete or the trial is censored.
mechanism_prediction: Median actor policy_grad_norm over windows 1-20 falls below 1/3 of trial 2's (~44 -> < 14.7). If the grad norm does not fall that much, value gradients were not the dominant actor signal, regardless of quality outcome.
falsification: Hypothesis 'shared-feature value gradients drive the drift' is falsified if the quality criterion fails or the grad-norm prediction fails.
after: No further recipe trials are admitted. If it passes, the paired fused-vs-8-bit protocol uses this recipe for both arms (rebased onto 637d1326). If it fails, report the baseline as unstable and stop.
